"CHOOSE WISELY’

Actress Jodi Sta. Maria recently advised her followers to "choose wisely," reflecting on how what we devote ourselves to ultimately shapes our character and identity.

She concluded her timely post with: "God bless the Philippines 🇵🇭 🙏🏼."

While widely loved for her classic roles like in "Please Be Careful With My Heart," Sta. Maria has become increasingly outspoken off-screen. Since calling for government transparency in her first rally back in September 2025, she has taken a firm public stand against corruption and the recent flood control scandals.

Her sociopolitical voice comes with notable background as she was previously married into a prominent political family. In June 2024, the Supreme Court officially granted the nullity of her marriage to Panfilo "Pampi" Lacson Jr., the son of Senator Panfilo "Ping" Lacson, putting an end to a 13-year legal battle.

(✍️: Rafael Asonza)

#radarPH
#radarEntertainment

Several emerging-market countries are strong candidates for incorporating Pi Network into their national economies—modeled after Bermuda’s Stellar integration—but only if Pi continues maturing its mainnet, smart contracts, stablecoin rails, and compliance in 2026–2027. This is not financial or political advice, but an objective analysis based on public data as of mid-2026.

Pi’s edge is its massive mobile-first user base (60+ million pioneers globally, 14–16+ million migrated to mainnet), low/zero-fee P2P payments via a Stellar-like consensus protocol, and focus on everyday commerce/remittances in the developing world. It could reduce merchant fees (often 3–10% on cards), cut remittance costs (global average ~6%), enable instant government disbursements, and drive inclusion without heavy infrastructure—exactly the pain points Bermuda cited.

 Selection Criteria
I prioritized countries where Pi already has critical mass (top user shares from community surveys, traffic data, and reports) + structural economic needs (high remittances as % of GDP or absolute inflows per World Bank data, large unbanked/mobile populations, payment friction in informal economies). Developed nations like the US or Germany were excluded: they have users but entrenched legacy systems make sovereign adoption far less practical.

Here’s the prioritized list (top-tier first):

1. Nigeria (Pi’s #1 market, ~10% of global users)  
   Africa’s crypto leader with a young, tech-savvy population and widespread smartphone use. High inflation, cash-heavy informal economy, and merchant fees create perfect conditions for low-cost digital payments. Strong community-driven merchant pilots and barter already exist. National adoption could instantly onboard millions of existing Pioneers for wages, remittances (~$20B+ inflows), and social services—leapfrogging traditional rails like Stellar did for Bermuda.

2. India (~9% of Pi users; world’s #1 remittance recipient at ~$129B)  
   Enormous population and digital inclusion push (UPI success shows government appetite for instant payments). Pi’s grassroots scale could complement UPI for cross-border remittances and rural merchant payments where card fees still bite. With millions of Pioneers already active, it offers a ready-made on-chain layer for financial inclusion without starting from scratch.

3. Philippines (~5% of Pi users; ~$40B annual remittances)  
   One of the world’s most remittance-dependent economies (OFW-driven). High mobile penetration and existing fintech momentum make Pi’s wallet-first model ideal for faster, cheaper inbound transfers and local merchant acceptance. Government has explored digital finance; Pi’s existing user base could accelerate a national “digital peso” layer for fees, wages, and disbursements.

4. Vietnam (top-3 Pi market, very active community)  
   Rapidly growing Southeast Asian economy with strong grassroots Pi adoption and tech clusters. Remittances and informal commerce are significant; Pi’s low-fee ecosystem aligns with government digital-economy goals. Active pioneers and merchant pilots already underway mean minimal adoption friction—similar to how Bermuda leveraged Stellar’s readiness.

5. Indonesia (~6% of Pi users)  
   Archipelagic nation with massive population, high smartphone use, and expanding digital economy initiatives. Southeast Asia’s “explosion” in Pi activity mirrors Vietnam. It could cut high inter-island and merchant transaction costs while enabling government payments and inclusion in underserved areas.

6. Brazil (notable user base in Latin America)  
   Large emerging market with high crypto interest, remittances, and informal economy. Pi’s mobile model fits Brazil’s fintech-friendly regulatory environment and could support merchant payments and social program disbursements at near-zero cost—addressing the same growth-hindering fees Bermuda highlighted.

Honorable mentions (strong secondary fits):  
- Ghana, Kenya, South Africa (growing African Pi communities + mobile-money precedents like M-Pesa; high inclusion potential).  
- Pakistan and Bangladesh (major remittance recipients with emerging Pi activity).  
- Mexico (top-3 global remittances; overlaps with Latin American Pi growth).

 Why These Countries—Not Others?
These nations combine immediate network effects (tens of millions of pre-existing Pi wallets) with real economic pain points that Bermuda’s Stellar move directly targeted: high fees, slow/expensive remittances, and the need for inclusive digital infrastructure. Pi’s protocol DNA (fast, energy-efficient, mobile-native) matches what a national payments layer needs, while its community scale gives it a “bottom-up” advantage Stellar lacked at launch.

That said, no country has announced Pi-based national plans yet (searches confirm zero sovereign partnerships as of May 2026—Pi’s 2026 focus remains ecosystem growth, dApps, and merchant tools). Success would require Pi to deliver proven on-chain volume, regulatory alignment (KYC already advancing), and stablecoin integration first. Smaller or highly remittance-dependent nations could pilot even sooner than large ones.

In short: Pi won’t replace Stellar-level institutional deals tomorrow, but in these high-adoption emerging markets, it has the unique user foundation to make a Bermuda-style national on-chain economy not just possible—but potentially transformative for everyday citizens and growth. Execution and policy will decide if any actually move forward.

#CriticalMass #GlobalUsers

✈️ FLYWINGS SHIFTS INTO EXPANSION MODE | AVIATION PLAY GETTING BIGGER

FLYWINGS SIMULATOR TRAINING CENTRE is no longer positioning itself as just a simulator training company.
The latest filing signals a broader aviation infrastructure and capability buildout.

🚀 Key Developments:

• IPO utilisation shifted towards leasing 2 A320NEO Full Flight Simulators for 10 years
• Strengthens advanced pilot training ecosystem
• New simulator facility planned at Panvel, Maharashtra
• ₹35.33 Cr pilot training infrastructure allocation remains intact

🛫 What stands out?

• Long-term simulator lease creates recurring training visibility
• Expansion beyond Gurgaon indicates scaling ambition
• Demand backed by airline pilot shortage and aviation growth

🏗 Bigger Strategic Shift:

Board approves entry into aviation infrastructure & EPC verticals including:

• Airfield & runway lighting systems
• Instrument Landing Systems (ILS)
• Air traffic advisory systems
• EPC & electro-mechanical works

⚙️ Also investing in advanced aviation equipment:

• Full Flight Simulators
• 6 DOF Motion Platform
• CEET 320 Equipment
• Cabin Visual & Slide Trainer

🧠 The interesting part is the transition:

From a training operator → toward an integrated aviation infrastructure & training platform.

As India’s aviation ecosystem expands, Flywings appears to be positioning itself deeper into the value chain. 🚀

SB19: P-Pop Kings Redefining Global Style

Photo Credits: 1Z Entertainment + Billboard Philippines + Mega Magazine + ITM. + VMan Southeast Asia

Origins: Forged in Fire

SB19 in school uniforms with umbrellas on grassy lawn 

In 2016, five young talents—Pablo Nase (leader), Josh Cullen Santos, Justin de Dios, Ken Suson, and Stell Ajero—entered a grueling survival show inspired by South Korean training camps. They endured physical drills, vocal bootcamps, and personality shaping under ShowBT Philippines, debuting as SB19 on October 26, 2018, with the heartfelt ballad "Tilaluha."

The early days were rocky. P-pop was nascent in the Philippines, and their debut barely registered amid K-pop's dominance. Yet, persistence fueled their spark—by 2019, explosive single "Go Up" ignited a movement, winning Song of the Year at the MYX Music Awards.
SB19 channels effortless charm on MEGA Magazine's cover, blending schoolboy whimsy with high-fashion edge.

Check out our article @ https://t.co/1NetKI82Hw
